title: Lie Routing Vision Language Models for View-Robust 3D Understanding
claim: Changing viewpoint makes model responses drift and performance drop across tasks, while view-aware routing keeps responses stable and accuracy higher.
layout: 2 rows: top scene, poses and heatmap grid; bottom three plots
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a) on top shows a reconstructed 3D indoor scene with a red box around a long table and the query 'This is a long table surrounded by chairs.' Next to it are a reference frame and a top-down camera-pose map with near, medium and far cameras. On the right is a 3×3 grid. Columns are Near, Medium and Far, colored green, orange and red. Rows are raw frames, heatmaps without routing and heatmaps with routing. The without-routing heatmaps become diffuse as the view gets farther, and the with-routing ones stay concentrated on the table. Panel (b) on the bottom has three scatter-plus-fitted-curve plots for 3D dense captioning (ROUGE), visual grounding (IoU) and object detection (F1@0.25), all against ΔR in degrees. The red baseline curve falls steeply and the green LieVLM curve stays higher, with faint shaded background regions.
caption: 3D scene viewpoint variation exposes semantic instability and downstream performance degradation. (a) Without routing, query-relevant activations become diffuse and less target centered across views, while Lie routing preserves stable target responses. Warmer regions indicate stronger support for the target phrase. (b) Fitted task trends show that performance degrades as sample-level viewpoint variation $\Delta R$ increases, while LieVLM maintains stronger performance across higher levels of viewpoint variation. For grounding, raw IoU visualizes the continuous quantity underlying Acc@0.5. Additional examples are provided in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have made substantial progress in 3D scene understanding from multi-view RGB observations. Yet a fixed object and query can elicit inconsistent target-related responses across camera viewpoints, a phenomenon we characterize as viewpoint-induced semantic drift. We introduce LieVLM, a Lie routing framework for view-robust 3D understanding. Motivated by the rotational component of viewpoint change, Lie routing adapts visual representations by applying local $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ transformations to projected features within learned three-dimensional subspaces. Geometry tokens extracted by VGGT predict local rotation parameters and channel-wise routing coefficients. A closed-form PadÃ©--Cayley map transforms projected visual features, whose identity-relative corrections are projected back and gated into the original visual and geometry features. This design retains the pretrained semantic and direct spatial context while learning view-dependent feature adjustments. Experiments on 3D captioning, grounding, detection, and spatial reasoning show consistent improvements over additive fusion across training scales and backbones. Controlled ablations examine the roles of geometric conditioning and transformation structure. Viewpoint analyses further reveal systematic variation in the predicted routing states alongside more localized target responses and stronger task performance across viewpoint changes.
